feedback: Judged from iteration 0 and the candidate's contents, not from any race of this candidate. In iteration 0 every run on all three development tracks ended off_track with one line-loss event each. Max_error was about 0.062, just past the 0.06 m limit, while rms_error stayed low at 0.026 to 0.029. That pattern points to a sudden departure at a bend rather than general sloppiness, so the speed and derivative changes are aimed at the right failure. The candidate is valid: all values are inside contract limits, the sensor count matches the weights, and geometry is unchanged, which is correct because the sensor layout is not the cause. The main risk is the time limit. Lowering base_speed from 1.8 to 1.5 reduces base PWM from about 0.90 to 0.75 of full, so completion_time may rise and the robot may fail to cover the course in 3.0 s, which would forfeit the 500-point completion bonus. This is a single, well-reasoned step that will show directly whether the sharp bend is the failure point, and there are ten iterations left, so approve it and read the telemetry before changing more. Interpret the next race as follows. If line_loss_events drop to zero and max_error falls below 0.06 but progress stalls short of the finish, raise base_speed toward 1.7 while keeping kd at 0.4. If line losses persist at the same bend, lower base_speed further or raise kd before touching kp. If the robot completes, record completion_time and tune speed up from there.
requested_changes: If the next race shows line_loss_events still at 1 on the sharpest bend, lower base_speed further (for example 1.5 to 1.3) before changing kp, since iteration 0 showed the failure is a departure at a bend.
If runs stay on track with max_error below 0.06 but completion is 0 and progress is low, raise base_speed from 1.5 toward 1.7 with kd held at 0.4, to recover completion_time within the 3.0 s limit.

If steering_oscillation rises above the iteration 0 level of about 0.14 to 0.16 after kd is raised to 0.4, reduce kd toward 0.3 rather than lowering kp, because kp 4.0 already gives a large steering range.
